newsitem.title: USA: Jury sentences Texas woman to death for killing son.
newsitem.headline: Jury sentences Texas woman to death for killing son.

text.p: A Texas jury on Tuesday sentenced a Dallas mother to die by lethal injection for the stabbing death of her five-year-old son.
Darlie Routier, 27, showed little emotion and kept her head down when the jury's decision was read. Family members wept softly as they left the courtroom.
No execution date had been set. All death penalty cases in Texas are automatically appealed.

Routier was convicted on Saturday of capital murder in the killing of her younger son Damon and faces a pending charge in the murder of her son Devon, 6. The boys were stabbed to death with a butcher's knife while they slept on June 6 in their Rowlett home near Dallas.
Routier is the seventh woman on Death Row in Texas but no woman has been executed in the state since 1863.

State District Judge Mark Tolle polled the jury to see if its decision, reached after four hours of deliberation, was unanimous. One by one, all of the jurors raised their hands to signify that it was.

In arguments on Tuesday, prosecutors urged the jury to sentence Routier to death because they said she was a continuing threat to society. "This is a woman capable of the unspeakable in her own home," prosecutor Greg Davis said, showing the jurors photographs of the boys.
Another prosecutor, Sherri Wallace, said society must protect its children by punishing those who harmed them.
"Darlie Routier, we are not going to tolerate what you have done to our children. You will die," she said.
But defence attorneys pleaded for a life sentence, which in Texas is the only alternative to the death penalty for a conviction of capital murder.
"You know that whatever you found happened that night was a one-time event that's beyond explanation. There's no continuing threat to society," defence attorney Richard Mosty told the jury.
Routier testified in the trial that an intruder killed the boys and attacked her, but police said they found no evidence of that.

Prosecutors charged that Routier killed her sons in a fit of anger at the family's financial difficulties and her ongoing weight problems. They portrayed her as vain and selfish, which defence witnesses denied.
The trial, which began on Jan. 6, was moved to Kerrville, 60 miles (100 km) northwest of San Antonio, Texas, because of heavy pre-trial publicity.
